answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when it is caught double-voting or breaking a verifiable task rule. Honest agents recover the stake, while an attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil account and risks losing it; creating names is cheap, but scaling coordinated fraud is not. A kernel of independent validators can check evidence, with disputes sampled across an ocean of tasks; an opal badge may signal reputation, but it should never replace the stake or proof.
